paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: We show the empirical generalization errors (termed Error in the figures) and estimated Hessian traces of the loss for fine-tuned adapters (using QAdapter on Llama-3-8B) across various hidden dimensions. Smaller adapters achieve the lowest generalization errors. Additionally, the Hessian trace values correlate with generalization errors, suggesting that smaller adapters tend to converge to flatter minima.
model_annotation: The plot titled “Errors (RTE)” illustrates how the error metric varies with adapter rank for the RTE setting. The x-axis is labeled “Rank” on a linear scale, with discrete tick labels at 4, 16, 64, and 256 (no intermediate labeled ticks). The y-axis is an unlabeled numeric error scale on a linear axis, spanning roughly from about 0.25 up to about 1.0, with labeled ticks at approximately 0.3, 0.6, and 0.9 (regular spacing of 0.3). A single series is shown as a thick solid black line connecting large filled green circular markers, with vertical black error bars (with caps) at each point. The series starts near 0.35 at rank 4 (error bar roughly ~0.28 to ~0.42), dips slightly to about 0.33 at rank 16 (~0.28 to ~0.39), rises to around 0.41 at rank 64 (~0.33 to ~0.49), and then increases more sharply to about 0.63 at rank 256 (~0.59 to ~0.67).
